# ERRORS.md — error / rejection surface of the C library

Mechanically generated by `gen_errors.py` from `c_src/src/*.c`.  Every
`js_error` / `js_typeerror` / `js_rangeerror` / `js_syntaxerror` /
`js_referenceerror` / `js_urierror` / `js_evalerror` call, every lexer
(`jsY_error`), parser (`jsP_error`) and compiler (`jsC_error`) error, every
`die()` in the regexp compiler, every `js_throw()` re-raise and every
`assert()` is listed.  One row per distinct (function, message template)
pair; `sites` gives every source line that raises it.

**240 distinct rejections** across **266** source sites.

How each class is observed from outside the `.so`:

* JS-level throws — `js_dostring` / `js_ploadstring` / `js_pcall` /
  `js_pconstruct` return non-zero and leave the error object on the stack;
  `js_trystring(J,-1,...)` renders it as `"<Type>: <message>"`.
* `die()` in `regexp.c` — `js_regcomp` returns `NULL` and stores the message
  in `*errorp`.
* `js_throw()` re-raise — the *pending* value propagates unchanged, so the
  observable result is whatever value was thrown.
* `assert()` — `abort()`; the trigger is outside the function's contract, so
  it is verified by showing both libraries reject/avoid the same domain
  rather than by calling it.

The `covered by` column is filled in from the Phase C trigger table in
`tests/c_errors.rs` (parsed by `gen_errors.py`), so a row can never be
silently left untested: `phase_c_coverage` fails if any row has no trigger,
and `phase_c_triggers_hit_their_rows` fails if a trigger does not actually
produce the message the row documents.
